subject: Acme Therapeutics — admin activity export & delivery options
messages:
From: Ava Collins <audit@acmetx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC2 evidence: admin activity export (scope: 2027-07-01 to 2028-06-30)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our SOC2 auditor has asked us to produce a vendor-supplied admin activity dataset covering all privileged admin actions for the period 2027-07-01 to 2028-06-30. Their requirements:
- a complete event-level export (no sampling) including timestamps, actor identifier, action type, target resource, IP, and change diff where applicable
- timezone-normalized timestamps (UTC) and timezone field preserved
- signed manifest (SHA256) and HMAC on each payload file
- redaction guidance for user-display names (we can accept stable hashed identifiers)
- delivery options: SFTP with public-key auth or AWS S3 assuming an SCP transfer to our secure bucket

I attached our SIG/SOC2 questionnaire with specific evidence points flagged (see pages 6–8). Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
1) produce a full export for the requested window in NDJSON or Parquet;
2) provide a signed manifest + HMAC;
3) perform minimal redaction (PII -> hashed id) before transfer; and
4) propose a transfer plan and estimated lead time?

We are aiming to close this by mid-July to keep our audit timeline.

Thanks,
Ava Collins
Acme Therapeutics — InfoSec (on behalf of SOC2 team)

Hi Ava —

Appreciate the detail and the questionnaire. Short answer: yes, we can deliver. High-level options:
- Full NDJSON export (line-delimited events) or Parquet bundles for efficiency
- UTC-normalized timestamps + original tz field retained
- Signed manifest (SHA256) and HMAC per file; we can provide verification instructions
- We can pseudonymize user display names to a stable SHA256(id + salt) prior to handoff; we do not alter retained audit metadata (actor id, role, action flags)

To finalize: can you confirm preferred transfer method (SFTP pubkey vs S3 role assumption) and whether your auditor needs us to include operator console session recordings (those are large and handled separately)?

I'll loop in eng + security to confirm rollup size/lead time and propose a delivery window.

Best,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2028 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: SOC2 evidence: admin activity export — Feasibility + ETA?

Marissa —

We can produce either NDJSON or Parquet. Tradeoffs: NDJSON is easier for auditors; Parquet cuts size ~3–5x and still preserves schema. For a full 12-month snapshot across privileged admin actions, rough estimate: 25–60M events depending on tenant counts and automation traffic. That maps to ~10–30GB compressed parquet, or ~60–120GB NDJSON compressed.

Technical notes / constraints:
- We'll generate per-day files (UTC) and provide a manifest with SHA256 hashes and an HMAC-SHA256 using a key we'll provision to you via a one-time secure channel (or you can provide a key).
- Pseudonymization: we will hash internal display_name -> SHA256(display_name + salt). We recommend customer-supplied salt to meet auditor independence; if they can't provide, we can use a per-account salt and document the process.
- Redaction: we won't redact action diffs by default; if they require content redaction we need scope examples (e.g., full request payloads vs only metadata).
- Delivery: S3 role-assume (preferred) or SFTP. For S3 we'll do a signed, time-bound role; for SFTP we'll push files to their endpoint.

ETA: If they accept Parquet + S3 role-assume + customer salt, we can schedule a dry run and provide sample files in 5 business days (2028-07-09). Full bundle by 2028-07-14. If they insist on NDJSON and need in-line diffs redacted, add 3–5 business days for rework.

I'll prepare a small sample (one day) NDJSON and Parquet file and a manifest (attached).

—Karthik
Staff Engineer — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Hi Ava —

Per the team: we can absolutely produce the requested export. Proposed plan (summary):
1) Transfer format: Parquet (preferred) with NDJSON sample on request — both available.
2) File cadence: per-day UTC files for the window 2027-07-01 -> 2028-06-30.
3) Pseudonymization: we recommend you provide a salt (preferred). If you cannot, we will use a documented customer-specific salt and note the process in our evidence package.
4) Integrity: SHA256 per-file plus a transfer manifest. We will produce an HMAC key and share via a one-time secure transfer (we can use the HubSpot secure file exchange or an S/MIME-protected email for keys).
5) Delivery: S3 role-assume preferred. If you require SFTP, please provide endpoint, username, public key and a preferred folder.
6) Attachments: sample NDJSON + manifest attached for your review.

Proposed timeline: dry run (sample day) delivered by 2028-07-09; full bundle delivered by 2028-07-14 assuming your salt or S3 access is provided by 2028-07-06. Please confirm transfer method and whether your auditor needs us to include console session recordings (we can supply session metadata but recordings may require separate negotiation and will be larger).

Next steps:
- Ava: confirm S3 vs SFTP and salt decision
- Ben: procurement coordination once transfer method confirmed
- Karthik/Kim: we'll lock schedule after Ava confirms

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

Best,
